strategy.summary: Float and mixed int/float input with dtype timedelta64[s] is treated as nanoseconds on the buggy commit 15b1dd913e3d and truncated to zero; the fix routes all-numeric data through the dtype's unit (matching to_timedelta(..., unit='s')). Reproduce by building pandas at the buggy commit and running the two added test functions, which should fail there and pass at the fixed commit.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 15b1dd913e3d the parametrized tests fail because Series/TimedeltaArray built from float or mixed int/float data with dtype timedelta64[s] yields values near zero (nanosecond interpretation truncated to seconds) instead of the seconds values expected from to_timedelta(data, unit='s'); on the fixed revision the same tests pass, with all cases equal to the expected seconds-unit arrays.
strategy.numerical_probe: pd.Series([1.5, 2.5, 90.0], dtype='timedelta64[s]') should hold 90 seconds for the last element; buggy output is 0 days.

input_output_examples.expected_output: values interpreted in seconds (90s retained for 90.0)

risks: The fix changes lib.is_integer_float_array from cdef to cpdef, so the buggy and fixed builds must be compiled from the exact commits; a stale Cython build will not reflect either revision and the transition may not appear.

Build requires compiling pandas Cython extensions, which needs a working compiler and a NumPy version compatible with the checked-out tree; NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython versions are unbounded in the evidence (no documented constraint or era ceiling), so the choice of the latest compatible versions is inferred, not documented.

The Float64 masked-array and object-with-pd.NA/None cases depend on pandas extension array handling, which may differ across pandas dependency versions; if the buggy behaviour only appears under a particular NumPy major version, the transition may not reproduce.
Known corners (1e10+0.5 raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta, object input like [Timedelta('1s'), 2.0]) are pre-existing and their behaviour is unknown; they are not part of the target test.
The bug is platform-independent in the evidence, but no platform or sanitizer requirement is stated; no architecture-specific behaviour is claimed.
Expected values for NaN/NaT in mixed input beyond the listed examples are not stated in the evidence; the test relies on comparison against the integer-based m8[s] reference with NaT.

oracle.reference_source: pandas integer-path m8[s] result and pd.to_timedelta(data, unit='s').as_unit('s') as encoded in the developer tests
oracle.why: Timedelta64 values in a given unit are integer-valued; the developer tests use assert_series_equal and assert_extension_array_equal, so equality is exact rather than tolerance-based.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 15b1dd913e3d the constructed Series/TimedeltaArray holds values truncated to zero (nanosecond interpretation of 1.5, 2.5, 90.0), so assert_series_equal / assert_extension_array_equal against the seconds-unit expected value raises an AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the float and mixed int/float inputs are interpreted in seconds and match the expected seconds-unit values exactly, so the assertions succeed.
